input.summary: Defect density rises monotonically with dose. For doses 1–3 (point-like, vacancy-type defects; Lorentzian fits of D and G, 532 nm) I_D/I_G is 0.25 → 0.57 → 1.19, giving mean inter-defect distance L_D ≈ 24 → 16 → 11 nm and n_D ≈ 5.5e10 → 1.3e11 → 2.6e11 cm⁻² (Cançado calibration, ±~30% systematic). Dose 4 is not a lower-defect state even though I_D/I_G drops to 0.58: D and G broaden to ~58 and ~45 cm⁻¹, G upshifts to 1591 cm⁻¹, 2D nearly vanishes (I2D/IG ≈ 0.07) and D′ merges into G. This is the amorphization (stage-2) regime, so the L_D formula does not apply. I can only say L_D is below ~3 nm, which means n_D is above ~1e12 cm⁻², and that is a bound rather than a measurement.

observations.finding: The D-peak intensity relative to G grows about 2.1× per dose step from dose 1 to 3, so the defect density rises strongly and roughly monotonically.
observations.evidence: Single-Lorentzian fits with a linear baseline. D at 1346–1347 cm⁻¹ (FWHM ~15 cm⁻¹, constant). G at 1580.3–1580.6 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 13.8–13.9 cm⁻¹, constant). I_D/I_G by height: 0.25 (dose 1), 0.57 (dose 2), 1.19 (dose 3). By area: 0.27, 0.61, 1.26. Both give the same trend.

observations.finding: The defect type in doses 1–3 is consistent with vacancy-like (point) defects, not sp3 functionalisation or grain/edge boundaries.
observations.evidence: I_D/I_D′ (height) = 6.2, 6.3, 6.9 for doses 1, 2, 3. D′ at ~1620–1621 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 11–13 cm⁻¹) is resolved from G. The ratio is nearly constant with dose. This is a modest-S/N estimate, since D′ height is only ~110–430 counts against noise ~50–70 counts rms.
observations.source: Eckmann et al., Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012), Fig. 4 and text: I_D/I_D′ ≈ 13 for sp3, ≈ 7 for vacancies, ≈ 3.5 for boundaries

observations.finding: Quantitative defect density for doses 1–3: L_D² = 1.8e-9·λ⁴·(I_D/I_G)⁻¹, which at 532 nm is L_D² ≈ 144 nm²/(I_D/I_G). The areal density is n_D = 10¹⁴/(π L_D²) cm⁻² ≈ 2.2e11 × (I_D/I_G) cm⁻².
observations.evidence: Dose 1: L_D ≈ 24 nm, n_D ≈ 5.5e10 cm⁻². Dose 2: L_D ≈ 16 nm, n_D ≈ 1.3e11 cm⁻². Dose 3: L_D ≈ 11 nm, n_D ≈ 2.6e11 cm⁻². Using area ratios instead gives values ~5% different. The calibration itself is ±~30%.
observations.source: Cançado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011), Eq. 5 and Fig. 3; Lucchese et al., Carbon 48, 1592 (2010)

observations.finding: The graphene is otherwise unchanged through doses 1–3: no detectable doping or strain change and no 2D degradation.
observations.evidence: G position 1580.3 / 1580.6 / 1580.4 cm⁻¹, G FWHM 13.9 / 13.8 / 13.8 cm⁻¹. 2D at 2689.8 / 2690.9 / 2690.1 cm⁻¹, FWHM ~32 cm⁻¹ in all three. I2D/IG = 3.02 / 2.98 / 2.97 and A2D/AG = 6.96 / 6.89 / 6.85. G near 1580 cm⁻¹ with a high 2D/G ratio is consistent with low doping. The single-Lorentzian 2D width (~32 cm⁻¹) is consistent with monolayer, but this is not a full 2D-shape analysis.

observations.finding: Dose 4 is in the amorphization (stage-2) regime, past the maximum of the I_D/I_G curve. Lower I_D/I_G here does not mean fewer defects.
observations.evidence: D 1351.7 cm⁻¹ with FWHM 58 cm⁻¹. G 1591 cm⁻¹ with FWHM 45 cm⁻¹ (up from 1580 and 14). D′ is at best a shoulder (fit 1610 cm⁻¹, FWHM 28 cm⁻¹, height ~160 counts). 2D collapses to a broad weak hump (FWHM ~129 cm⁻¹, height ~216 counts vs ~7400–10700 for doses 1–3; I2D/IG = 0.07). I_D/I_G = 0.58 (height) or 0.75 (area). The baseline also becomes sloped and broad, with a possible D+D″ background near 1100–1200 cm⁻¹ and 2D/D+G features that are weak and broad. Taken together this is nanocrystalline or disordered carbon with L_D likely below ~3 nm. I_D/I_G in this regime scales roughly with L_a², and the Cançado L_D formula is invalid.
observations.source: Ferrari & Robertson, Phys. Rev. B 61, 14095 (2000), amorphization trajectory (Fig. 2); Lucchese et al., Carbon 48, 1592 (2010), Fig. 3: I_D/I_G peaks at L_D ≈ 3 nm then decreases

observations.finding: The sharp narrow lines are not graphene defect features and do not affect the analysis.
observations.evidence: Si first-order peak at ~520 cm⁻¹ from the substrate, present in all spectra. A narrow spike at ~2170 cm⁻¹ in dose 2 only, consistent with a cosmic-ray event (one pixel-scale spike). It lies outside all fit windows.

properties.value: 1 (monolayer, per the preparation; consistent with I2D/IG ≈ 3 and a single-Lorentzian 2D width ~32 cm⁻¹ in doses 1–3). Not independently checked beyond that.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: low to medium for dose 1 (ID/IG 0.25), medium for dose 2 (0.57), high for dose 3 (1.19), and very high (amorphous or nanocrystalline) for dose 4.

properties.name: L_D_nm
properties.value: ≈24 (dose 1), ≈16 (dose 2), ≈11 (dose 3), and <~3 for dose 4 (formula not applicable; bound only)
properties.source: Cançado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011), Eq. 5; Lucchese et al., Carbon 48, 1592 (2010)

properties.name: n_D_cm-2
properties.value: ≈5.5e10, 1.3e11, 2.6e11 (doses 1–3, ±~30% systematic); dose 4 above ~1e12 cm⁻² (rough bound)

properties.name: defect_type
properties.value: vacancy-like point defects (I_D/I_D′ ≈ 6–7)
properties.source: Eckmann et al., Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012), Fig. 4

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: none detectable in doses 1–3 (G and 2D positions constant within ~1 cm⁻¹). The dose-4 G upshift is attributed to disorder, not strain.

properties.name: doping_type
properties.value: no change detectable in doses 1–3. Absolute doping level not determined (G ≈ 1580 cm⁻¹, FWHM ≈ 14 cm⁻¹, 2D/G ≈ 3 suggests low doping).

caveats: The Cançado calibration was derived for Ar⁺-bombarded graphene at 2.41 and 2.33 eV. It assumes point-like defects and a mostly uniform distribution. Other treatments (plasma, e-beam, chemical) may have a different calibration constant, so n_D is accurate to roughly a factor of 1.5. The relative trend, a factor of ~2 per step, is more reliable than the absolute values.

Dose 3 (I_D/I_G ≈ 1.2) is approaching the maximum of the curve. The 1/L_D² law is already starting to saturate in this range (Lucchese et al.: the peak is at L_D ≈ 3 nm). The dose-3 density could therefore be underestimated, and the stage-1 assignment rests on the sharp G (FWHM 13.8 cm⁻¹) and the unchanged 2D/G.

For a single spectrum, I_D/I_G is ambiguous between the stage-1 and stage-2 branches. Dose 4 would give a deceptively low L_D-based defect density if the formula were applied (I_D/I_G 0.58 → L_D ≈ 16 nm, identical to dose 2), which is wrong. The broad lines, G upshift and 2D collapse are what identify it as stage 2.

The fits are single Lorentzians with a linear baseline and no propagated uncertainties. The ratios carry a few-% fit uncertainty from noise (~50–70 counts rms), more for the weak D′ and for the dose-4 hump, where the baseline is sloped and the D/G/D′ lines overlap heavily. In dose 4 a 3–4-component fit (D, G, D′, D″) would be more appropriate. The D′ ratio at dose 1 (height ~110 counts) is especially uncertain.

Absolute intensities differ between spectra (e.g. G height 2800, 3600, 2500) because of focus, spot position and the changing optical interference on SiO₂. Only intensity ratios are used. The sample was not necessarily at the same spot, so local inhomogeneity (the 100× spot samples ~1 µm²) is mixed into the dose trend.

The laser (1 mW, 532 nm) on a defective graphene flake can anneal or add defects (and heat the sample) during acquisition. The 2D position and width show no sign of heating or drift, but a power series was not done.

Si 520 cm⁻¹ is intense, so the focus is partly in the substrate. This does not change the ratios, but the baseline in the 900–1000 cm⁻¹ region contains second-order Si, which should not be mistaken for graphene defect features.
Raman cannot separate defect types uniquely. The I_D/I_D′ ≈ 6–7 assignment to vacancies is indicative and depends on S/N and on the D′ fit.
questions_for_user: What is the treatment (ion species/energy, plasma, e-beam, chemical) and what are the actual dose values? The Cançado calibration was done for Ar⁺, and with real doses I could check whether n_D scales linearly with dose (my numbers imply a roughly 2× increase per step).
Were all four spectra taken at the same spot, or were multiple spots averaged? Spot-to-spot variation in D/G on the flake would change the uncertainty on the L_D values.
Was there any vacuum or air exposure, annealing, or time delay between treatment and measurement? Reactive defect sites (sp3/H or O functionalisation) can change I_D/I_D′ and the defect type.
What are the laser spot size and the acquisition time per spectrum? I want to rule out laser-induced annealing or damage, and to estimate how many defects the spot samples.
Do you have a pristine (dose 0) reference spectrum? It would give the intrinsic doping and strain baseline, and it would show whether the exfoliated flake already had an I_D/I_G above zero.
citations: Cançado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011): Quantifying defects in graphene via Raman spectroscopy at different excitation energies (Eq. 5, Fig. 3).
Lucchese et al., Carbon 48, 1592 (2010): Quantifying ion-induced defects and Raman relaxation length in graphene (Fig. 3, I_D/I_G vs L_D).
Eckmann et al., Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012): Probing the nature of defects in graphene by Raman spectroscopy (I_D/I_D′ ratios, Fig. 4).
Ferrari & Robertson, Phys. Rev. B 61, 14095 (2000): Interpretation of Raman spectra of disordered and amorphous carbon (amorphization trajectory, Fig. 2).
limits: Cannot give an absolute defect density with better than ~±30–50% because the calibration is treatment-dependent. Dose-to-dose relative values are more reliable.
For dose 4 the data give only a bound (L_D < ~3 nm, n_D above ~1e12 cm⁻²), not a number.

Cannot tell the exact chemical nature of the defects (vacancy vs. functional groups, hydrogenation vs oxidation) from a single excitation wavelength. A wavelength- or polarisation-dependent set, or XPS/STM, would be needed.
Cannot tell spatial distribution (uniform vs clustered/edge-localised defects) from one spectrum per step. The same-spot assumption is untested.
Cannot resolve small changes in doping or strain at the ~1 cm⁻¹ level without a G–2D correlation analysis with proper uncertainties. None was done here beyond peak positions.

Dose 3 (I_D/I_G ≈ 1.2) is approaching the maximum of the curve. The 1/L_D² law is already starting to saturate in this range (Lucchese et al.: the peak is at L_D ≈ 3 nm). The dose-3 density could therefore be underestimated, and the stage-1 assignment rests on the sharp G (FWHM 13.8 cm⁻¹) and the unchanged 2D/G.

For a single spectrum, I_D/I_G is ambiguous between the stage-1 and stage-2 branches. Dose 4 would give a deceptively low L_D-based defect density if the formula were applied (I_D/I_G 0.58 → L_D ≈ 16 nm, identical to dose 2), which is wrong. The broad lines, G upshift and 2D collapse are what identify it as stage 2.

The fits are single Lorentzians with a linear baseline and no propagated uncertainties. The ratios carry a few-% fit uncertainty from noise (~50–70 counts rms), more for the weak D′ and for the dose-4 hump, where the baseline is sloped and the D/G/D′ lines overlap heavily. In dose 4 a 3–4-component fit (D, G, D′, D″) would be more appropriate. The D′ ratio at dose 1 (height ~110 counts) is especially uncertain.

Absolute intensities differ between spectra (e.g. G height 2800, 3600, 2500) because of focus, spot position and the changing optical interference on SiO₂. Only intensity ratios are used. The sample was not necessarily at the same spot, so local inhomogeneity (the 100× spot samples ~1 µm²) is mixed into the dose trend.

The laser (1 mW, 532 nm) on a defective graphene flake can anneal or add defects (and heat the sample) during acquisition. The 2D position and width show no sign of heating or drift, but a power series was not done.

Si 520 cm⁻¹ is intense, so the focus is partly in the substrate. This does not change the ratios, but the baseline in the 900–1000 cm⁻¹ region contains second-order Si, which should not be mistaken for graphene defect features.
Raman cannot separate defect types uniquely. The I_D/I_D′ ≈ 6–7 assignment to vacancies is indicative and depends on S/N and on the D′ fit.

Was there any vacuum or air exposure, annealing, or time delay between treatment and measurement? Reactive defect sites (sp3/H or O functionalisation) can change I_D/I_D′ and the defect type.
What are the laser spot size and the acquisition time per spectrum? I want to rule out laser-induced annealing or damage, and to estimate how many defects the spot samples.
Do you have a pristine (dose 0) reference spectrum? It would give the intrinsic doping and strain baseline, and it would show whether the exfoliated flake already had an I_D/I_G above zero.
